salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness and mass in the ear canal, consistent with schwannoma

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen and cartilage on gross examination, suggestive of chondrosarcoma

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and myxochondroid matrix on microscopic examination, consistent with pleomorphic adenoma

shortlist.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal and expansion of the fallopian canal, possible hemangioma

shortlist.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Location near the stylomastoid foramen and geniculate ganglion, possible hemangioma

raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of an irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma. The tumor's location and the patient's symptoms suggest involvement of the facial nerve, which is a common site for schwannomas.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While the pathology report mentions cartilage, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic adenomas are typically found in the salivary glands, not in the temporal bone or associated with the facial nerve.

rejected.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
rejected.why: Hemangiomas are typically vascular lesions, but the imaging findings and pathology report do not suggest a vascular tumor.

rejected.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
rejected.why: The location of the tumor is not consistent with a geniculate ganglion hemangioma, which would be expected to be more proximal in the facial nerve.
